content.text: Found it — the Pixel 8 Pro (serial `<REDACTED-1>`) has BenchTarget installed. I'll target that device for all measurements.

The `open` tool reports a `startup.durationMs` field — exactly what's needed. This first launch may not have been from a guaranteed cold state though, so I'll redo it properly: force-stop, then launch, five times.

## Cold-start measurements — dev.lincforge.benchtarget (Pixel 8 Pro, serial <REDACTED-1>)

Each run: force-stopped the app (`close`), then launched it fresh (`open`), reading the `startup.durationMs` from the launch round-trip.

| Run | Cold-start time (ms) |
|-----|----------------------|
| 1   | 3470 |
| 2   | 3105 |
| 3   | 3246 |
| 4   | 3607 |
| 5   | 3334 |

**Median:** 3334 ms
**Mean:** 3352.4 ms
**Sample standard deviation (n-1):** ≈ 194.6 ms (variance ≈ 37,881 ms²)
**Population standard deviation (n):** ≈ 174.1 ms (variance ≈ 30,305 ms²)

Note: timings are measured via the tool's `open` command round-trip (launch request → app foregrounded), which includes some IPC/tool overhead on top of pure Android `ActivityManager` start latency — treat as a consistent relative measure across runs rather than an exact `am start -W TotalTime` figure.
